system_prompt: You are a research coder for the Global Government GenAI Observatory (G3O), a public, auditable dataset that measures how government institutions worldwide adopt generative AI. You read one web page, or one part of one, about a named institution and answer coding questions about it. Use only what the text says: record what it states explicitly and never infer, guess or use outside knowledge. Give each answer in the form the question asks for and nothing else: for a question with listed answers, choose from those answers only; for an extraction, copy the exact words from the text.

questions.instructions: Code this PAGE for the named institution only, using only what the page says. Does it document a generative-AI activity at this institution? If several values fit, take the first in this order.

criteria.text:
The page documents a specific generative-AI activity AT THIS institution: its own GenAI tool, pilot, policy or guidance on GenAI, procurement, deployment, or institution-directed staff GenAI training. The text must be explicitly generative AI (LLMs, ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini, AI chatbots, AI-generated content or equivalents) and tied to this institution, not only to a national programme or another body. The activity must be carried out or adopted by the named institution itself. Exclude activity by a parent, higher-level or neighbouring body (e.g. a district, county, regency, region, consortium or city department when the named institution is a village, ward or sub-unit), by a similarly named organisation or company, and pages by vendors that only use the place name. Generic 'AI', 'artificial intelligence', 'smart' systems, automation, analytics, prediction, transcription, translation, image or video recognition, or traditional machine-learning tools do not count unless the page says the tool generates text, images, audio, code or other content, or names a generative product or model (e.g. ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini, Claude, an LLM, an AI chatbot or AI assistant).

Rules:
1. `not_assessable` is not one of the answers: it is set when a page was not reviewed.
2. A tool the page calls an "AI chatbot" or "AI assistant" counts as generative AI, even where a rule-based chatbot would otherwise be excluded.
3. Translation counts as generative AI only when the page ties it to a named generative product or says a language model produces it.
4. A public-facing GenAI event or educational programme is not a qualifying activity; an event page can support a separate record only when it documents the institution's own adoption, procurement, deployment or governance.
5. An activity carried out by an organisational unit of the named institution (department, office, service) counts for the named institution. An activity of its parent, a sibling, or a separate court, board or authority does not, unless the page says the named institution takes part.
6. A joint activity counts when the page names this institution as a participant.

The page mentions AI at this institution, but it cannot be settled whether it is generative AI (e.g. a generic 'AI strategy', 'AI tools', analytics, traditional machine learning).

questions.instructions: What kind of document is this page?

criteria.text:
The page is, or is one entry in, a structured list of AI or algorithmic systems kept by a government body, with several entries in a common format (inventory, register, catalogue, algorithmic transparency record in a standard template), **and the list covers more than one institution** (a national or sectoral register, a standard-template record series across agencies).

Rules:
1. Any government-kept multi-entry list in a common format counts as a register, including one institution's own list; single-institution and cross-institution registers are separate values. `disclosure_scope` still codes whole-of-government vs multi-institution for cross-institution registers; `register_single_institution` must carry `disclosure_scope` = `single_institution` (QC check).
2. The obligation must be named on the page, except that it may be inferred from the document's genre **when the document's title names AI or algorithmic reporting**. Otherwise a statutory annual report or a compliance report under a rule not about AI is `formal_record`.
3. (1) A city's entry in a national algorithm register describing its chatbot → `register_cross_institution`. (2) A ministry annual-report section headed with the regulation that requires AI-use reporting → `mandated_report`. (3) Council minutes approving a Copilot licence → `formal_record`. (4) A mayor's press release launching a chatbot → `informal_official`. (5) A trade-press article about that chatbot → `third_party`. (6) A city web page that lists its five AI tools in a table it made itself → `register_single_institution`.
4. A document produced to meet a reporting obligation that concerns reporting on AI, algorithms or digital systems (statutory annual-report section, compliance or transparency report under a rule). The obligation must be named on the page, except that it may be inferred from the document's genre when the document's title names AI or algorithmic reporting. Otherwise a statutory annual report or a compliance report under a rule not about AI is formal_record.
5. The page's kind cannot be determined from its text (e.g. an archived fragment with no header).

questions.instructions: Does the page name a person, office or unit as responsible for a GenAI activity it mentions, or for questions about it?

criteria.text:
The page gives a named person, office or unit as responsible for the activity or for questions about it; a named official with no contact details counts.

Rules:
1. Items: `content_purpose` (what the tool is used for), `content_tool_or_model` (product or model named), `content_vendor` (supplier named), `content_data` (data inputs or data handled described), `content_users` (who uses it or who is affected), `content_status_date` (deployment status or date stated), `content_contact` = yes if either sub-item is yes: `content_contact_named` (a named person, office or unit given as responsible for the activity or for questions about it; a named official with no contact details counts) and `content_contact_details` (contact details anywhere on the page: email address, phone number, postal address or contact form, including press or vendor contacts and site footers). `content_purpose`, `content_tool_or_model`, `content_vendor`, `content_users` and `content_status_date` are derived, not asked: each is yes when any activity on the page has a value stated on the page in its matching activity field (purpose: the activity's function items; tool or model: tool or model name; vendor: model developer, stated or looked up, or contracting party; users: `target_users` or `governed_population`; status or date: `adoption_stage` or a year field), otherwise no. `content_data` is asked about any GenAI activity on the page. The five derived items and `content_data` apply only on pages whose page verdict is one of the five GenAI-bearing values; on other pages they are `no`.
